audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer assigns Volibear's stun to his E in five separate places ('his E stun', 'his E (the slow overhead paw-slam stun)', 'his E-stun engage', 'his E hand-of-the-god stun'). Riot's kit puts the stun on Q, Thundering Smash — 'gains speed towards enemies, Stunning and damaging the first one he Attacks'. E is Sky Splitter, a 1200-range lightning bolt that slows and shields him.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction of the matchup: Ragnarok's disable immunity answers Thundering Smash, and the whole level-6 plan is 'bait the Q stun'. A player told to dodge an E wind-up will sidestep the wrong ability and eat the one that actually locks him.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash (Q) is the stun, 12s at rank 1; Sky Splitter (E) is a 16s slow-and-shield he can drop from 1200 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gives Skill at Levels 1, 4-5 and 6 and Olaf at two-plus items, while whys[0], whys[3] and whys[4] all say Olaf wins those stages and whys[6] says Volibear out-scales.
audit.why: The prose, the packet chart and a 53.72% win rate all describe an Olaf-favoured lane that tilts back at two items. The chart says the opposite at both ends.
audit.corrected: Olaf rows 1 through first item; Skill at two-plus items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes never give a cooldown; the packet reports the abilities are never named at all in the full layer.
audit.why: Volibear's punishable windows are numeric: Thundering Smash 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, Sky Splitter a flat 16s, Stormbringer 160s at rank 1. Frenzied Maul at 5s is the one thing he always has, which is why it is a sustain problem and not a trade window.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to the spike, the Do's entry and the cooldown block.

audit.why: Anti-heal is correctly flagged as core — Frenzied Maul's second cast heals him and it is only 5s.
53.72% over 901 games matches the Olaf-favoured early framing.

edits.before: Ragnarok makes you immune to his E stun — his only peel is dead while you E him down or dive.
edits.after: Ragnarok answers Thundering Smash, his Q stun on 12s — his only lockdown is dead while you dive.

edits.before: Ragnarok cleanses his E stun mid-fight, so his only hard-CC peel does nothing while you E him down — dive him under tower.
edits.after: Ragnarok answers Thundering Smash — his Q stun is his only hard CC and it is 12s, so bait it, press R and dive him.

edits.before: Voli's biggest threat window — he out-scales you with tank items and his E-stun engage reclaims the brawl once your true damage falls off.
edits.after: Voli's biggest threat window — tank items plus a 5s Frenzied Maul heal reclaim the brawl once your flat true damage stops mattering.

edits.before: Voli is a tanky even-brawler, but you out-trade him 1-3 because your E is guaranteed true damage that his armor and W bite-heal can't soak. Land Q to slow him, walk up for an auto, and weave E when he steps to last-hit — your passive ramps your attack speed as you take the trade back. Dodge his E (the slow overhead paw-slam stun) by sidestepping when he winds up; that stun is the only thing that flips a trade against you.
edits.after: Voli is a tanky even-brawler, but you out-trade him 1-3 because Reckless Swing is true damage his armour and Frenzied Maul heal cannot soak. Land Undertow to slow him, walk up for an auto, and swing when he steps to last-hit — your passive ramps attack speed as you drop low. The ability that flips a trade is Thundering Smash, his Q stun on 12s: sidestep that wind-up, not Sky Splitter, which only slows and shields him.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you keep snowballing short trades — axe-reset Q perma-slows him so he can't disengage, and W omnivamp out-heals his bite. At 6 you hit a wall-breaker: Ragnarok cleanses and is immune to his E stun, so the one ability he needs to peel or all-in does nothing while you chase. Force the all-in or tower-dive here; bait his E first, then ult and E him into the dirt.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you keep snowballing short trades — the axe pickup refunds Undertow's 9s cooldown so he can never disengage, and your passive life steal answers his bite. At 6 you hit a wall-breaker: Ragnarok's disable immunity eats Thundering Smash, the Q stun that is his only hard CC, so the ability he needs to peel or engage does nothing. Bait that 12s stun first, then ult and run him down or dive.

edits.before: Land his E hand-of-the-god stun to lock your all-in before you E him
edits.after: Land Thundering Smash, his Q stun, to lock your all-in before you swing

edits.before: Use Q empowered dash + R tower disable to dive you back once he out-tanks you
edits.after: Use Stormbringer's leap and tower disable to dive you back once he out-tanks you

edits.before: His engage. R cleanses it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Thundering Smash is 12s — bait the stun, then run your pattern.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Frenzied Maul is 5s and heals on the second bite — anti-heal it.

edits.before: - Volibear Thundering Smash: matchup-defining — His engage. R cleanses it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Thundering Smash: matchup-defining — his Q stun, 12s at rank 1, and Ragnarok answers it. Bait it, then commit. - Sky Splitter: 16s, slow and shield from 1200. - Frenzied Maul: 5s, heals on the second bite.

notes: The E-is-the-stun error also appears in fields I did not rewrite (late: 'his E-stun engage'), because rewriting late would have required changing more than the length band allows around unrelated claims; the corrected fact is recorded in the audit so a later pass can finish it. Chart flips are matched full/content pairs and land as one group.
